subject: Sidecar boundary mapping & SOC 2 diagram request
messages:
From: Auditor - Veridian Inc <sig-auditor@veridian.com>
To: kimberly_park@redwood.com
Date: 2026-08-16T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Request: network diagram and sidecar boundary for SOC 2 assessment

Hi Kimberly,

Following our kickoff, the SOC 2 reviewer asked us to provide a concise network diagram that highlights the sidecar/agent boundary between control-plane processes and customer inference workloads for Dedicated and Private deployments. Specifically we need:

- A diagram showing where sidecars (logging/telemetry, policy agent, KV-cache proxy) live relative to the inference runtime and GPU pools.
- A dataflow table indicating which channels cross tenant boundaries and which are strictly control-plane-only.
- Any compensating controls (e.g., egress ACLs, per-tenant KMS scoping, mutual TLS with cert boundaries).

Can you share these artifacts and an evidence index by EOD Tuesday? We only need redacted diagrams for high level — no PII.

Thanks,
Alex Ramos
Sig & Compliance, Veridian Inc

--

Subject: Re: Request: network diagram and sidecar boundary for SOC 2 assessment

Kimberly — I reviewed the draft topology. Notes below (internal):

- Sidecar placement: we run lightweight sidecars in the same pod/instance namespace as the inference container for observability and policy enforcement. They are namespaced per-tenant on Dedicated via enforced pod annotations; on Private the sidecars are customer-managed at the VPC boundary when requested.
- Control plane endpoints: health, orchestration, and model registry access use a separate control-plane VPC (peered) or dedicated management subnet. No customer data flows to the control-plane except metadata (job ids, telemetry pointers) — we mark those as pseudonymous.
- KV-cache proxy: runs on inference host for low-latency and is bound to a tenant token. Access is strictly over mTLS; ACLs restrict cross-tenant token use.
- KMS: we support both Redwood-managed KMS (multitenant HSM with strict tenant key wrapping) and customer-managed KMS via external key referencing. We'll include wording rather than key material.
- Egress: default deny; explicit egress rules for telemetry endpoints; third-party integrations require allowlisting per-customer.

Action items: Michael, can you add a one-paragraph kernel/cgroup isolation blurb we can include in the evidence index? I will assemble a redacted diagram and CSV dataflow matrix for Veridian.

-M
From: michael_grant@redwood.com
To: marissa_cole@redwood.com, kimberly_park@redwood.com
Date: 2026-08-18T16:47:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Request: network diagram and sidecar boundary for SOC 2 assessment

Short kernel note — drop-in for SOC 2 pack:

Redwood runtime enforces inference process isolation using Linux cgroups and user namespaces. On Dedicated hosts we pin inference processes to isolated NUMA nodes and create a dedicated container sandbox per customer with enforced seccomp and restricted capabilities. The GPU driver exposes per-process contexts and we use MIG (where supported) to carve hardware-level isolation. Sidecars run as separate containers with network namespaces tied to the same pod; IPC and filesystem mounts are minimized and access-controlled.

I'll attach the kernel blurb to the evidence index. Kim/Marissa — once you sign off I can export the diagrams as redacted PDFs and upload the index.

-Michael

Attachments referenced (to be uploaded): sidecar_boundary_diagram_v1.pdf; dataflow_matrix_v1.csv; soc2_evidence_index.md
